title: Ooga Booga
subtitle: A contest across volcanic islands
summary: Ooga Booga is Visual Concepts' multiplayer action game, released for Dreamcast in North America on 11 September 2001.
body: Ooga Booga is Visual Concepts' multiplayer action game, released for Dreamcast in North America on 11 September 2001. Players control Kahunas competing for the favour of a volcano goddess across island arenas. Thrown heads, staffs, spells and rideable animals supply a deliberately comic collection of attacks. The four basic characters favour different strengths, from speed to magic, making the choice of fighter part of the contest. Local and online multiplayer put those abilities into direct competition, with the island's creatures and structures offering further opportunities to interfere with rivals.

Boars and birds can be ridden, changing how a player moves through the arena. Tikis provide another useful target: claiming one makes it attack opposing players and their own Tikis. A match therefore involves more than chasing the nearest rival. A helpful animal or captured structure can change the balance, giving somebody away from the main fight a way to return with an advantage. Unlockable characters and islands extend the choices, while the exaggerated movements and attacks keep the contest readable as a shared comic spectacle.

The game arrived near the end of Dreamcast's commercial life and became one of its last original online releases. Visual Concepts was better known on the console for sports games, making this small-scale arena contest a different use of its multiplayer experience. Brian Luzietti and Larry Peacock composed the music. The appeal lies in the temporary opportunities around the island: a rival may appear stronger in a direct exchange, but a mount, spell or newly claimed Tiki can quickly turn the next encounter into a different contest.
